evals.prompt: A repo whose tests use Docker compose stacks. Following only the fleet skill, (1) write the exact dispatch prompt for issue #42 "Add retry", worktree /w/repo-issue-42, base feat/retries, size s, files internal/retry.go; (2) list exactly what reconcile does to tear down issue #42's worktree and any containers/volumes it started after its PR merges.
evals.expected_output: The dispatch prompt names no Docker or COMPOSE_PROJECT_NAME line. Reconcile tears down only via `tp remove <branch> --merged` and says the repo's treepad remove hook owns cleanup of anything the worktree started; fleet names no technology.

evals.prompt: Follow dispatch.md for label `demo` with three ready, non-tiny tickets: #10, #11 and #12 all name internal/app.go and the golden directory testdata/golden/. Say how each worktree is based, what runs in parallel, each prompt's Base, and what the final report tells the user about merging.
evals.expected_output: No chains: all three worktrees are created up front from origin/feat/demo and run in parallel, and every prompt has Base: feat/demo. There is no merge simulation or rebase step. The report lists PRs in issue order, then runs `fleet land demo --check` and, on `land`, tells the user to review each PR and run `/fleet land demo` before merging; on `reconcile`, to merge the PRs in order and run `/fleet reconcile demo`.

evals.prompt: Follow dispatch.md for label `demo` with three ready, non-tiny tickets: #10, #11 and #12 all list internal/app.go under Files to touch. Say what dispatch does about the shared file and what the final report says about it.
evals.expected_output: Dispatch runs `fleet hotspots demo` and does no overlap analysis of its own. All three tickets still dispatch in parallel off origin/feat/demo. The report lists internal/app.go as a hotspot with #10, #11 and #12 and suggests a refactor ticket to split it.

evals.prompt: Follow land.md for label `demo`. The wave has three PRs into feat/demo: #20 and #22 are ready for review, #21 is still a draft. `fleet land demo` prints one line per PR with status `ok`, then `ready 3` on stdout. Say what you run, what you tell the user, and whether you merge anything.
evals.expected_output: Runs only `fleet land demo`, with no git or gh commands of its own, and merges nothing: the draft #21 was prepared like the others. Tells the user the order to squash-merge #20, #21 and #22 into feat/demo, notes the compare links land commented, and recommends `/fleet reconcile demo` afterwards.

evals.prompt: Follow reconcile.md for label `demo`. `fleet reconcile demo --state <scratchpad>/fleet/state.md` prints `unfinished issue-20/add-retry issue-22/add-cache` on stdout and `closed-unmerged #21` on stderr. Say what you run, what you tell the user, and whether you raise the feature PR.
evals.expected_output: Runs `fleet reconcile` once, with no gh label moves or blocker parsing of its own. Runs `tp remove issue-20/add-retry --merged` and `tp remove issue-22/add-cache --merged` and no other removals. Does not raise the feature PR because the line says unfinished. Reports #21 as needing the user's decision and ends by telling them to /clear and run `/fleet dispatch demo`.

evals.prompt: Follow land.md for label `demo`. #20 and #21 both edit the body of `Parse` in internal/app.go. `fleet land demo` prints a line for #21 with `pull-in=#20 needs-work` and the terminal line `needs-work #21` on stdout. Say what you do next, and what happens when the subagent returns `#21 resolved rewrite <report>` versus `#21 failed rewrite <report>`.
evals.expected_output: Spawns exactly one fresh subagent for #21, never the ticket's own, briefed with the plan path and PR number, both PRs' intent, the worktree via `tp` and `[checks] pre_push`, and told to merge origin/feat/demo and #20's tip into the branch (no rebase, no force-push). It does not hand the conflict to the user first. On `resolved` it re-runs `fleet land demo --resolved "#21 resolved rewrite <report>"`. On `failed` it records the line the same way, which prints `gate-failed #21 resolver-failed`; it then names #21 and any `blocked-by #21` PRs, hands them to the user, spawns no second subagent, and still recommends reconcile.

evals.prompt: Follow land.md for label `demo`. Two PRs into feat/demo, #30 and #31, both regenerate the same testdata/golden/ directory, so #31 conflicts with #30 only in generated files. `fleet land demo` logs `regen #31: <command>` on stderr and prints `ready 2` on stdout. Say what you run, whether you spawn a subagent or merge anything by hand, and what happens next.
evals.expected_output: Runs only `fleet land demo`, with no git or gh commands of its own. Spawns no subagent and merges nothing by hand: #31 was regenerated by the CLI. Treats `ready 2` as both PRs mergeable in order with a green suite, tells the user to squash-merge them in order, and recommends reconcile.

evals.prompt: Follow land.md for label `demo`. `fleet land demo` prints `gate-failed #31 just lint` on stdout. A second run prints `regen-stale testdata/golden/out.txt`. For each, say what you tell the user, what you run next, and whether you reconcile.
evals.expected_output: For both lines it reports to the user and stops: gate-failed names PR #31 and the failing `just lint` command, regen-stale names testdata/golden/out.txt as out of date. It spawns no subagent and edits no files itself. It still recommends reconcile once the user has merged what they chose.
